title: The Incredible Speed of Unpleasant Situations
author: Admired Leadership
summary: This article contrasts the slow build of good outcomes with the sudden onset of bad ones, arguing that leaders' instinct to match crisis speed with fast reactions is usually the wrong move. It identifies reacting too quickly as the number one sign a leader is letting a bad situation spiral. The prescription is counterintuitive: slow down, gather full facts about what happened and who's affected, before responding at all. The piece closes with the idea that a leader's credibility is defined by the quality of their response, not the crisis itself.
points: Good outcomes take time to build; bad situations erupt suddenly and catch leaders unprepared.
Reacting too quickly is identified as the number one sign a leader is losing control of a bad situation.
The right response is to slow down and gather a complete assessment before acting.
Responding before all the facts are in usually forces leaders into multiple, credibility-eroding follow-up responses.
A leader's credibility is defined by their response to a crisis, not by the crisis itself.
quotes: Bad things, on the other hand, happen quickly, often by surprise.
The speed of bad things must be matched by a slowness in response.
Taking the time to gather all the facts surrounding the situation is the better call.
The best leaders recognize their credibility is always defined by their response to the situation, not by the event or episode itself.
